newsitem.title: ITALY: Under half of Italy's euro-tax based on income tax.
newsitem.headline: Under half of Italy's euro-tax based on income tax.

text.p: The government plans to raise some 5.5 trillion lire of the so-called euro-tax from a one-off levy on personal income tax, officials from the federation of self-employed workers said after meeting ministers.

The euro-tax, which forms part of the government's controversial 1997 budget, is designed to raise a total 12.5 trillion lire to help Italy qualify for European economic and monetary union at the start in 1999,
"From what we understood, around 5.5 trillion lire will come from income tax, which will be considered as a loan," federation chairman, Ivan Spallanzani, told reporters.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi is meeting leaders of Italy's three main trades unions and is due to hold a news conference shortly. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
